rows.source_population: 30 UK primary-care patients aged >=50 years (60% aged >=75 years) interviewed on symptom recognition and path to atrial fibrillation diagnosis

rows.note: Same older-adult (>=75 years) atrial fibrillation population; verbatim everyday arrhythmia phrase 'irregular heartbeat' reported from patient interviews.

rows.note: Same oral-lithium severe hand-tremor side-effect context ('shakes' used verbatim), adapted from a first-person adult lithium patient quote (cohort mean age 43.1 years) to an adult-child carer describing a 70-year-old father.

rows.expression: a little bit of a shudder in the hands

rows.source_population: UK adults aged 37-84 years (mean 58.2 years) treated with a plaster cast or wrist splint for a distal radius fracture

rows.source_population: parents of children with Tourette syndrome interviewed at a children's hospital in western China (translated quote from Parent P3)

rows.expression: and I think it's a habit

rows.source_population: 17 adult outpatients with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia interviewed on recurrent nosebleed frequency, duration, and intensity

rows.source_population: 10 older adults aged 60-81 years with actinic keratosis interviewed in Sweden 4 weeks after photodynamic therapy

rows.note: Same older-adult (ages 60-81 years) actinic keratosis population using verbatim descriptor 'scaly and red', adapted from patient descriptions of post-PDT treated skin to untreated chronic actinic scalp lesions.

rows.source_population: 114 primary-care outpatients aged >50 years (mean age 71 quantitative, 69 qualitative) reporting nocturnal leg cramps

rows.note: Same older-adult primary-care nocturnal leg cramp population (mean age 69-71 years vs age 70); verbatim phrase 'leg cramps' used directly.

rows.source_population: adult patients referred for syncope-spectrum complaints ('blackouts', 'loss of consciousness', 'falling out', 'passing out', 'fainting') at the Nashville, Tennessee Veterans Administration Hospital
rows.family_population: 70-year-old colloquial English speaker with a physician-monitored 4 cm abdominal aortic widening who had a sudden syncopal blackout 15 minutes ago
rows.note: Same adult US clinical syncope-evaluation population using referral complaint 'blackout(s)' in the medical syncope sense (matching core entry 'blackout / blacked out' in dialect_lexicon_20261109.json).

rows.source_population: English speakers using colloquial/dialect adjective 'swimmy' for dizziness (Wiktionary lexical entry 'swimmy', Adjective sense 1; attests lexical sense only)
rows.family_population: 22-year-old colloquial English speaker with persistent dizziness ('swimmy headed') and unsteadiness on fast turns 2 months after bumping the head in soccer despite a primary-care doctor evaluation
rows.note: Wiktionary dictionary sense ('Dizzy; swirling or moving as if seen in a daze', matching core entry 'swimmy headed / my head feels swimmy' in dialect_lexicon_20261109.json) attests general lexical meaning rather than a post-head-impact vestibular cohort; combined into 'swimmy headed'.

rows.expression: a misery in the right side of my chest
rows.source_population: US and UK dialect English speakers using noun 'misery' for bodily pain (Wiktionary lexical entry 'misery', Noun sense 2; attests lexical sense only)
rows.family_population: 44-year-old US or UK dialect English speaker with 6 days of right-sided chest wall pain ('a misery in the right side of my chest') aching on rib pressure after getting over a cough last week
rows.note: Wiktionary dictionary sense ('A bodily ache or pain' in US and UK dialects, matching core entry 'a misery in my chest (or side, or back)' in dialect_lexicon_20261109.json) attests regional dialect lexical meaning rather than a post-tussive chest-wall pain cohort; instantiated as 'a misery in the right side of my chest'.

rows.source_population: 24-year-old woman in New Delhi, India prescribed outpatient antibiotic therapy for diarrhea ('loose motions') who subsequently developed drug-induced lip angioedema (case report)
rows.family_population: 33-year-old Indian English speaker with 14 days of mild belly bloating and loose motions 4 times daily after returning from a camping trip
rows.note: Both involve young-adult Indian English outpatients seeking treatment for 'loose motions' (used verbatim, matching core entry 'loose motions' in dialect_lexicon_20261109.json), adapted from clinician case-report prose focused on subsequent antibiotic angioedema to a first-person 14-day post-camping diarrhea presentation.

rows.source_population: 48-year-old man in Canada presenting with a linear plant-contact forearm eruption ('an itchy rash') initially diagnosed as poison ivy dermatitis
rows.family_population: 29-year-old adult with a mild 3 cm linear itchy rash on the right ankle 2 days after brushing against poison ivy while hiking
rows.note: Same adult linear plant-exposure contact dermatitis context (poison ivy / poison-ivy-simulating plant contact); verbatim symptom phrase 'an itchy rash' used directly.
